answer: Require each agent to prove a unique passport with a zero-knowledge proof, threading one document to one identity like a willow root holding one trunk. Step one, the operator scans the passport NFC chip and makes a ZK proof hiding all personal data. Step two, the proof carries a nullifier, so the same passport can never register a second agent. Step three, duplicate nullifiers are rejected on-chain and the stake is slashed. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 passports at about $150 each, $150,000 plus forgery charges. A passport is an ivory tower of trust: one document, one agent, no copies.
